title: Quarterly Uptime, Spend & Pilot Handoff - Redwood / Halcyon Health
summary: QBR-style health check focused on uptime, token spend, and next-phase pilot handoff. Reviewed last quarter usage trends, cost overrun drivers, P95 latency spikes during peak, and proposed optimizations (batching, prefix cache, model quantization). Agreed next steps: security package + SOC2 evidence, run a 24h throughput benchmark on Dedicated pool, and pilot kickoff week of Dec 8.

Customer: confirm pilot workload and success metrics (by 2025-11-27)
CSM: set weekly check-in cadence during pilot

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-20 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood CSM), Alex (Halcyon CTO), Maya (Halcyon Lead ML Eng), Samir (Halcyon Infra), Nora (Halcyon Product)

Auto-summary: quick QBR + pilot handoff; some transcription noise, might miss a couple of proper nouns.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. Quick agenda: run through last quarter health - usage/costs/reliability, then priya will walk some optimization suggestions, then pilot scope and next steps.
[00:18] Alex (Halcyon): Yep thanks, we'll try to be concise. Main asks: 1) why did our token spend jump in Oct, 2) any quick wins for p95 tail, 3) timeline for pilot.
[00:30] Priya (Redwood SE): quick context, we pulled your runbook and saw a 3.7x increase in gen tokens from Sept to Oct, looks like bursty traffic across two endpoints and a lot of short-turnaround calls that don't hit the prefix cache. There were also a few large diffs when you switched model variants mid-month.
[00:52] Maya (Halcyon): yeah that aligns — we rolled a larger instr prompt and forgot to switch the cache policy. oops. Also some of our routings were hitting hosted vs dedicted, so mixed pricing.
[01:10] Jordan: right, we can optimize routing to prioritize Dedicated for steady traffic and routed fallback to Hosted for spikes. That should smooth unit cost. Also Priya has a quant/ batching plan.
[01:28] Priya: quick numbers — your P95 token latency is ~180ms on average, P99 spiking to 420ms during the 11/02 incident window. We see KV cache misses, and small sequence lengths are causing higher per-token overhead. With batching and tuned quant (int8-ish profile we tested) we project 22%-28% cost reduction and modest latency improvement at p95.
[01:54] Samir (Halcyon): can you confirm quantization won't change output fidelity? Our NER and downstream QA are picky.
[02:05] Priya: yes, that's our main caution. We'll start with a quantized variant in A/B canary and run your eval suite (the same prompt set you shared). If regressions >1% we hold. We can also use Redwood Optimize profile that keeps keys for critical routes unquantized.
[02:28] Nora (Halcyon): on reliability, the 11/02 incident — was that infra or model? We saw a lot of 500s then.
[02:36] Liam (Redwood CSM): short version: it was an autoscaler misconfig for a dedicated pool that caused a brief capacity blip and routing fallback to hosted endpoints; that ended up adding latency and some throttles. We've patched the policy and added extra headroom for your account.
[02:55] Alex: ok thanks. Were any requests lost? we saw some errors from our job queue.
[03:02] Priya: there were retries, but the platform's graceful fallback kept requests alive; we did log some 500s but no data loss. we'll send the incident packet.
[03:20] Jordan: action item — we'll share the incident report and updated autoscaler config.
[03:26] [00:03:30] Maya: about the cost spike — do you have a per-million-token unit cost comparison hosted vs dedicated?
[03:33] Jordan: yes, rough numbers (hand-wavy): hosted generation ~ $0.95 / 1M tokens at your tier, Dedicated effective cost ~ $0.52 / 1M tokens when amortized over your committed capacity. Embeddings slightly different. We'll attach a detailed slide.
[03:54] Samir: what about peeked memory and KV cache sizing for a dedicated pool? we want guidance for capacity planning.
[04:02] Priya: we recommend a Dedicated cluster for the main steady routes (2-4 GPUs to start), with a burst policy to hosted. KV cache size depends on your average context re-use; from your traces 70% of traffic had prefix reuse, so even modest cache (8-16GB per pod) yields big wins.
[04:23] Alex: on security/compliance — we need SOC two evidence, KMS integration, audit logs and SSO SAML for the Private control plane. What's in scope?
[04:34] Jordan: we have a security pack — SOC2 report, pen test summary, architecture diagrams for VPC/private, and KMS integration notes. We'll share the package and a one pager for the legal team.
[04:47] Nora: also need data residency notes — our legal wants data at rest region guarantees.
[04:53] Jordan: yes we support region pinning for Dedicated/Private and can sign residency terms in the ELA.
[04:59] [00:05:10] Priya: pivoting to pilot — propose pilot scope: 2-week staged pilot, start with a canary of 10% traffic on Dedicated config, run synthetic ramp to mirror peak 11/02, collect latency/cost/regression metrics. Success criteria: <=5% cost delta vs projected savings, p95 under 250ms, no functional regressions on eval prompts.
[05:26] Maya: 2 weeks sounds fine; does Redwood provide a dedicated SE for the bench itself?
[05:31] Priya: yes I will own the bench and run the workload with your infra team. We will need sample traffic and a test harness — Samir, you'll provide L7 traces and the job patterns.
[05:43] Samir: can do. We'll also provide the traffic replay tool we use.
[05:47] Jordan: timeline — Redwood to share SOC pack by Tue Nov 25, Priya to propose bench windows (target: week of Dec 1), customer to confirm pilot workload by Nov 27, pilot kickoff week of Dec 8.
[06:02] Alex: what about SLA uplift if pilot succeeds? we may need 99.9%+ for some routes.
[06:09] Liam: we can map to Dedicated SLA tiers and also offer latency SLO add-ons; we'll surface exact SLA language in the addendum.
[06:18] [00:06:30] Nora: pricing question — are there termination clauses for committed capacity? our CFO wants flexibility.
[06:25] Jordan: we have standard reserved commitments with early-exit clauses at a pro-rated fee; we can discuss in the commercial review. I'll flag finance to join if needed.
[06:36] Maya: small ask — can we get a low-friction way to switch routing rules mid-rollout? during our last rollout we had to manually toggle.
[06:44] Priya: yes, Redwood Console (our consoel spelled wrong in some logs) has routing policies you can change via API and we can pre-stage a canary toggle for you. We'll demo that in the bench.
[06:59] [00:07:15] Alex: any blockers you foresee?
[07:20] Priya: the main technical blocker is evaluating model fidelity under quant. the other is getting a clean traffic sample for bench. Both are solvable in the next week.
[07:31] Jordan: quick recap of commitments and owners, then open floor.
[07:36] Liam: recap: send SOC2 and incident packet (Jordan), bench schedule and quant plan (Priya), traffic traces (Samir), pilot playbook (Liam).
[07:48] Alex: ok looks good. Anything else?
[07:52] Maya: one more — can we get a short doc on debugging p99 tail latency? our on-call folks would use it.
[07:59] Priya: yes we'll add a troubleshooting runbook for p99 causes and mitigations.
[08:07] Jordan: cool, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench and a short deck. Thanks all.
[08:14] [End transcript — some lines truncated by auto-timestamping and ASR errors]

Notes: transcription includes occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "Redwood Consoel" instead of Console; "SOC two" for SOC2). Links shared: security pack (link placeholder), pricing sheet (link placeholder), pilot playbook template (link placeholder).
